Parents as Teachers is for Expecting Parents through Parents of Preschoolers from CDR in Greater Williamsburg Area

ByOlivia Bada 3 August, 20263 August, 2026

Parents as Teachers for Expecting Parents through Parents of Preschoolers from CDR in Greater Williamsburg Area and Surry County

✨ Parents as Teachers (PAT) – Supporting Local Families ✨

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:41
Instaread

A child’s early years are the most important for learning. Parents as Teachers (PAT) helps families overcome obstacles that can get in the way of early learning and empowers parents to be their child’s first and most important teacher. PAT staff can also link families to community resources that can help support them during and after their pregnancy.  A mother can receive help or support for breastfeeding in the home or during breastfeeding support groups. Once born, the baby can receive screenings and help with health and development with PAT staff. 👉 Learn more

PAT can assist with:

  • 🍎 Eating/nutrition
  • 🏡 Household routines
  • 🚗 Car seat safety
  • ⚠️ Finding hazards
  • 🚑 Preparing for emergencies
  • 🩹 First aid
  • 🎲 Play and development
  • 🙂 Child behavior
  • 🗣️ Language
  • 💡 Thinking skills
  • 🏃 Movement
  • 👨‍👩‍👧 Determining family needs
  • 🎯 Setting goals and steps

Who: PAT can help families until their child turns six years old.

What: PAT provides information, support, and encouragement to help children reach their full potential during their most critical years of life.

Where: Families take part in twice-monthly home visits and can attend parent groups and playgroups.

How:

  • PAT helps families access health care, understand child development and behavior, and use play activities to promote learning.
  • Home visitors screen for child development, health, hearing, vision, and safety needs.
  • PAT also supports pregnant families with prenatal development, health, nutrition, and newborn care.

📧 For more information about Parents as Teachers, contact:
Parents as Teachers Director Tracy Moler: tracym@cdr.org
👉 Learn more

In addition to Parents as Teachers (PAT) our Circle of Parents (COP), Williamsburg facilitators have recently extended group offerings to include Surry County.  

Circle of Parent’s “vision is a world where all caregivers have the knowledge, skills and support to raise strong, resilient, and happy children” and Child Development Resources is committed to fostering these relationships in our communities.  

Surry-based Circle of Parents groups meet weekly and are unique because they are parent-led, where each member can “find and share support” with one another and foster connectivity. COP is for all caregivers (grandparents, foster parents, etc.) with children of any age. Child-friendly activities are available and light snacks and drinks provided!  

Contact: Arianna Reynolds, ariannar@cdr.org        Parent Educator: Surry

PAT home visitors can help families find resources such as:

  • 🧑‍⚕️ Doctors/health care
  • 💉 Immunizations
  • 🛡️ Insurance
  • 🧑‍🏫 Counselors & therapists
  • 🥫 Food, clothing, supplies
  • 🧒 Child care/preschools
  • 🚗 Transportation
  • 🏠 Housing
  • 🎓 School or trade programs

Parents can help by:

  • 👀 Watching/observing
  • 👂 Listening/learning
  • 🧩 Thinking/problem-solving
  • 🙌 Participating
  • 💬 Communicating
  • 💡 Being open
  • 👩‍👩‍👧 Attending parent/playgroups
  • 🎉 Attending events
  • 📝 Giving feedback
  • ❤️ Helping other families
  • 👉 Learn more

🌟 Circle of Parents 🌟
What is Circle of Parents?
It’s a free, parent-led support group where caregivers can share ideas, find encouragement, talk about challenges, and support one another. No judgment — just real conversations, connection, and growth. This CDR group focuses on parents of children ages 3 to 6 years. This group is a space to:

  • Share parenting wins and struggles
  • Learn new strategies and perspectives
  • Connect with other local families
  • Build confidence as a parent

📧 Contact for Circle of Parents:

  • Nick Corsi – nickc@cdr.org
  • Lewi Blosser – lblosser@cdr.org

📞 Or call 757.566.3300 👉 Learn more
